newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific ups 1996 budget to $975 mln.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific ups 1996 budget to $975 mln.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group said on Friday it had increased its 1996 capital budget by $160 million to $975 million.
The increase was based on strong results in the company's drilling programs, Union Pacific said in a statement.
About 70 percent of the additional funds would be set aside for drilling and to buy land in the Austin Chalk, Gulf Coast and West Texas business units, it said.
The remaining 30 percent of the money would be used to develop gas value chain investments and for property purchases, Union Pacific said.

"While the investments related to this increase in our capital budget will be funded in 1996, the benefits to production and income will begin, for the most part, in 1997," President and Chief Executive Jack Messman said.
Union Pacific said it also recently finalized a $2.3 million purchase of producing properties, including 9,600 acres and ownership interest in 24 producing wells, from Enserch Exploration Inc.
